analysis.summary: The 1,028-page Form 20-F PDF exceeded the extraction limit so only narrative sections — not the financial statements — were captured; revenue, NPAT, EPS and operating cash flow cannot be stated with confidence and are marked n/a. What is clear: copper crossed 50% of Group Underlying EBITDA for the first time at a ~70% EBITDA margin, record WAIO iron ore output was achieved, and net debt fell to US$8.7bn. Dividends surged 56% to 172 USc/share (US$8.7bn total distribution), signalling strong cash generation and management confidence. The single biggest forward risk is commodity price volatility — particularly any copper demand softness from a US-China trade slowdown — combined with Jansen potash project execution risk ahead of mid-CY2027 first production.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- **Source limitation:** The Form 20-F runs to 1,028 pages; the text extraction provided covers only the front matter, Chair/CEO reviews, OFR narrative sections 1–3 and partial section 5 headers. The financial statements (page F-1 onwards), segment P&L tables and cash flow statements were not captured. All dollar P&L metrics are therefore marked n/a — this is a data availability issue, not a BHP performance issue.
- **Copper milestone:** For the first time, copper contributed >50% of Group Underlying EBITDA at a ~70% EBITDA margin; BHP remains the world's largest copper producer at ~2 Mt attributable output.
- **Record production:** WAIO achieved record annual iron ore production; Olympic Dam hit a 20-year copper production record; BMA stripping volumes were highest in five years.
- **Dividend surge:** Total FY26 ordinary dividend of 172 USc/share is up 62 USc (+56%) on FY25's 110 USc, implying underlying profit grew materially and the board is comfortable with the balance sheet.
- **Balance sheet tightening:** Net debt declined to US$8.7bn at 30 June 2026 (per footnote in OFR 2), a positive trajectory though the absolute quantum warrants monitoring given Jansen capex ahead.

## Key numbers
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Underlying EBITDA margin (Copper) | ~70% | n/a | n/a |
| Statutory NPAT | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Underlying NPAT | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Underlying EPS | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Ordinary dividend/share | US172c | US110c | +56% |
| Total shareholder distribution | US$8.7bn | n/a | n/a |
| Operating cash flow | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Free cash flow | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Net debt | US$8.7bn | n/a | n/a |
| Copper production (attributable) | ~2 Mt | ~2 Mt | flat |

*Note: Financial statement tables were not available in the extracted text. Investors should refer to OFR section 5.3 and Additional Information section 2 of the full 20-F for complete figures.*

## Quality of earnings
- Cannot be assessed quantitatively from the extracted text. The narrative references no unusual one-offs in FY26 operating performance.
- The completion of the Antamina silver streaming transaction (US$4.3bn) and WAIO power infrastructure agreement (US$2.0bn) — totalling US$6.3bn of capital unlocked — will likely appear as significant non-operating inflows or deferred revenue items in the statutory accounts. Investors should verify whether any portion of these transactions inflated reported profit vs underlying.
- Dividend coverage: 172 USc/share on ~5.081bn shares = ~US$8.74bn in dividends declared. BHP states this represents 50%+ of underlying attributable profit under the CAF, implying underlying attributable profit of at least ~US$17.5bn — but this cannot be confirmed from the extracted text.
- The WAIO power infrastructure deal and Antamina streaming are capital recycling, not operational earnings — their treatment in the income statement vs balance sheet is critical to assess earnings quality and should be verified in Note 33 (Significant Changes) and relevant transaction notes.

## Management framing
**Rating: Promotional — but not misleading**
- The Chair and CEO reviews lead with the fatality at Peak Downs (July 2026, post period-end) — appropriate and transparent.
- The narrative heavily emphasises copper's milestone (>50% of EBITDA), record production at multiple assets, and cost discipline without disclosing specific numbers in these sections — creating a bullish tone that cannot be independently verified from the extraction.
- The 172 USc dividend and US$8.7bn distribution figure are prominently cited as proof of financial strength — mathematically consistent with the 50% payout ratio policy implying ~US$17.5bn+ underlying profit.
- Jansen's cost and schedule update is mentioned neutrally ('updated shareholders on cost and schedule') without disclosing the magnitude of any cost increase or delay — this is a notable omission in the narrative sections.
- The 'US$6.3bn of capital unlocked' framing for the streaming/power deals is promotional language for asset monetisation; investors should scrutinise whether these transactions impair long-term earnings streams.
- Nickel is conspicuously absent from growth narratives — the Nickel West situation (which has been loss-making) appears to receive minimal positive framing, consistent with ongoing operational challenges in that segment.

## Segments
- **Copper:** >50% of Group Underlying EBITDA for first time; ~70% EBITDA margin; ~2 Mt attributable production; Olympic Dam 20-year record; Escondida record material moved and concentrator throughput despite grade decline. Escondida New Concentrator EID submitted March 2026, FID expected CY2027-28.
- **Iron Ore (WAIO):** Record annual production; lowest-cost major globally for seventh consecutive year; >US$10/t cost advantage over nearest Pilbara competitor; target >305 Mtpa by Q4 FY28.
- **Coal (BMA):** Open-cut production increased; highest stripping volumes in five years. NSWEC exceeded production guidance.
- **Nickel:** Referenced only in 'Other assets' section (OFR 4.4); no positive narrative in CEO/Chair reviews — likely still loss-making or in care-and-maintenance transition.
- **Potash (Jansen):** First production mid-CY2027; expected >60% earnings margin at steady state; ~10% of global potash supply potential. Cost/schedule update mentioned without specifics.
- Segment-level revenue and EBITDA tables not available in extracted text.

## Balance sheet
- Net debt: US$8.7bn at 30 June 2026 — stated in OFR 2 footnote; direction of travel (declining) is positive.
- US$6.3bn of capital unlocked via Antamina silver streaming (US$4.3bn received) and WAIO power deal (US$2.0bn agreement with GIP) will have materially supported cash and reduced gearing in FY26.
- Jansen Stage 1 capex remains in execution; the capital profile into FY27 and beyond will pressure free cash flow.
- Covenants, debt maturity profile and liquidity headroom not available from extracted text — refer to OFR 5.4 and Notes 21-24.
- The CAF minimum 50% payout ratio provides an implicit floor on dividend but also limits balance sheet conservatism in a downturn.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- Ordinary dividend: 172 USc/share for FY26 (interim + final), up 62 USc (+56%) from FY25's 110 USc.
- Total distribution: US$8.7bn across ~5.081bn shares.
- Payout ratio: ≥50% of underlying attributable profit (CAF policy) — implying underlying attributable profit ≥~US$17.5bn.
- No special dividend declared (or mentioned) for FY26.
- Share buybacks: Directors' Report section 4 references share capital and buy-back programs; details not available in extracted text.
- Capital unlocked via streaming/infrastructure deals (US$6.3bn) suggests active portfolio management to fund growth without excessive leverage.
- Franking status of dividends not specified in extracted narrative sections.

## Guidance and outlook
- **Copper production:** ~2 Mtpa maintained; growth aspiration ~5% p.a. CuEq from FY27 to FY35 (attributable copper business); overall Group copper-equivalent production growth target ~3-4% p.a. FY27-FY35.
- **Iron Ore:** >305 Mtpa (100% basis) target by Q4 FY28.
- **Jansen:** First potash production mid-CY2027; specific cost and schedule details not disclosed in narrative — investors should refer to OFR 4.5 and major projects section.
- **Escondida New Concentrator:** FID expected CY2027 or CY2028; 230-270 ktpa production target CY2031-32.
- **FY27 unit cost guidance:** Every major asset achieved FY26 unit cost guidance; FY27 guidance not detailed in extracted text.
- **No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided** in the extracted sections — consistent with BHP's standard practice of providing production and cost guidance rather than earnings guidance.
- Macro outlook described as 'resilient despite commodity market volatility' with 'strength in US and China'; cautious but constructive tone on trade dynamics.

## Positives
- **Copper dominance:** >50% of EBITDA at ~70% margin from the world's largest copper producer — structurally advantaged in the highest-conviction future-facing commodity.
- **Record production:** WAIO record iron ore output; Olympic Dam 20-year copper record; BMA highest stripping in five years — operational momentum is real.
- **Cost discipline:** Every major asset achieved unit cost guidance in FY26 despite inflation and supply chain pressure.
- **Dividend up +56%:** 172 USc implies very strong underlying profit growth and management confidence in cash sustainability.
- **Net debt falling:** US$8.7bn net debt with US$6.3bn of capital recycled — balance sheet in solid shape.
- **WAIO cost leadership:** >US$10/t advantage over nearest Pilbara competitor for seventh consecutive year — durable structural moat.
- **Copper growth pipeline:** Escondida new concentrator, CSA expansion, Spence sustaining growth, Vicuña and Resolution milestones — sector-leading pipeline with 5% p.a. CuEq growth aspiration to FY35.
- **Antamina silver streaming (US$4.3bn):** Realised significant upfront capital for a non-core by-product stream — intelligent capital recycling.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Fatality (post period):** Contractor death at Peak Downs in July 2026 — reputational, regulatory and operational risk; new CEO's first priority.
- **Jansen cost/schedule update without specifics:** The narrative acknowledges an update was made to shareholders on cost and schedule without disclosing the quantum — likely negative; investors must check the full OFR 4.5 and major projects section for the actual numbers.
- **Nickel silence:** Nickel West barely mentioned in the positive narrative — consistent with ongoing structural losses in a challenged nickel market; no clarity on strategic resolution.
- **Escondida grade decline:** Record throughput at Escondida was needed to 'offset the impact of an anticipated decline in ore grade' — grade dilution is a long-run headwind until the new concentrator ramps up post-CY2031.
- **FID not yet taken on Escondida concentrator:** Despite being the centrepiece of the copper growth strategy, FID is CY2027-28 — significant capital commitment and execution risk remain ahead.
- **Streaming/infrastructure deals reduce long-term earnings:** US$4.3bn Antamina silver streaming and US$2bn WAIO power deal provide upfront cash but forgo future silver revenue and potentially increase long-run power costs — the NPV tradeoff deserves scrutiny.
- **Financial statements not available in extracted text:** The 1,028-page document truncation means investors relying on this analysis alone cannot verify revenue, profit, margin or cash flow trends — refer to the full 20-F.
- **Copper price cyclicality risk:** With copper now >50% of EBITDA, BHP's earnings are more concentrated in a single commodity than at any point in recent history — a copper price correction would have outsized impact.

## Bottom line
**Bull case:** Copper at record prices with ~70% EBITDA margins, record production, disciplined costs, a 56% dividend increase and declining net debt all point to BHP firing on all cylinders. The pipeline (Escondida concentrator, CSA expansion, Jansen) offers 3-4% p.a. compounding CuEq production growth through FY35 with improving commodity mix. At this margin profile and with the world's largest copper position, BHP deserves a premium multiple.

**Bear case:** Copper price mean-reversion would devastate earnings now that copper is >50% of EBITDA. Jansen's undisclosed cost blowout is a known unknown. Nickel is a drag with no clear exit. Escondida grade decline is structural until ~CY2031. The Antamina streaming and WAIO power deals sold future earnings for upfront cash — a sign management was optimising the balance sheet ahead of heavy capex, not a sign of surplus capital.

**What would change the view:** (1) Full financial statements confirming the implied ~US$17.5bn+ underlying profit and cash conversion rate; (2) Jansen updated cost-to-complete and schedule — any further blowout is a material negative; (3) Copper price trajectory — a sustained move below US$3.50/lb would require a full re-rating of the earnings base; (4) Clarity on Nickel West — sale, closure or continued subsidy of the segment.
